title: A closer look at NGC 7314 nuclear region: a multiwavelength analysis of the Seyfert nucleus and its surroundings
question: To identify the main ionization mechanisms in the nuclear and circumnuclear regions of NGC 7314 within a radius of about 300 pc, study the AGN emission and variability, and analyse the gas kinematics.

recipe.goal: Reduce and treat GMOS optical IFU data cube and subtract stellar/AGN continuum
recipe.method: Reduce raw GMOS data in IRAF, correct for differential atmospheric refraction, combine via median, apply Butterworth spatial filtering, remove instrumental fingerprint, perform Richardson-Lucy deconvolution, and subtract continuum using STARLIGHT spectral synthesis.
key_parameters: spaxel size = 0.05 arcsec; Butterworth filter order n = 2, cut-off = 0.2 Ny; deconvolved PSF FWHM ~ 0.42 arcsec
assumptions: Galactic extinction AV = 0.058 with Cardelli et al. (1989) law; redshift z = 0.00476; MILES stellar library plus AGN power-law continuum with spectral index 1.5

recipe.goal: Align multiwavelength datasets (GMOS, HST, ALMA, SPLUS) and map emitting regions and kinematics
recipe.method: Remove cosmic rays from HST images using L.A.Cosmic, match HST filters on nuclear peak, align GMOS broad Halpha peak with HST F814W peak and ALMA CO(3-2) kinematic centre, and construct emission-line maps, channel maps, and Gaussian velocity/dispersion maps.
assumptions: Emission peak in HST F814W, GMOS broad Halpha peak, and ALMA CO(3-2) kinematic centre all correspond to the AGN position

recipe.goal: Decompose optical emission lines and measure fluxes and line ratios in Regions 1, 2, and 3
recipe.method: Extract spectra from Regions 1, 2, and 3; decompose narrow lines into blueshifted and redshifted Gaussians using the [S II] doublet as an empirical width/redshift template, plus broad Gaussians for BLR emission; correct for interstellar extinction via Balmer decrement and repeat decomposition.
key_parameters: 100 Monte Carlo iterations for uncertainty estimation
assumptions: [S II] and [N II] lines are emitted by the same partially ionized region with similar widths and radial velocities; Cardelli et al. (1989) extinction law

recipe.goal: Model photoionization and shock heating of narrow and coronal line regions
recipe.method: Generate grids of photoionization models with CLOUDY v13.03 to reproduce observed emission-line ratios in Regions 1, 2, and 3, and compare asymmetric components in Regions 2 and 3 with pure shock-heating models from the Mappings III library.
key_parameters: AGN continuum spectral index = 1.5; AGN bolometric luminosity = 2.5 x 10^43 erg s^-1; electron densities from [S II]6716/6731 at T = 10000 K; free parameters: filling factor, chemical abundances, low-energy cut-off, and (for Region 1) distance and CLR density
assumptions: T = 10,000 K for [S II] density calculation; bolometric correction of 600 for [O III]5007; distance from AGN equals projected distance for Regions 2 (2.8 x 10^20 cm) and 3 (4.0 x 10^20 cm)

recipe.goal: Model the broad Halpha line profile in Region 1 to derive BLR geometry
recipe.method: Fit a toy model of two circular rotating ring-shaped regions around the SMBH to the broad and very broad Halpha components.
key_parameters: Free parameters: radius (r), inclination (i), and Gaussian width (sigma_Gauss) of each rotating ring
assumptions: SMBH mass = 1.74 +/- 0.26 x 10^6 M_sun; circular Keplerian rotating rings

recipe.goal: Reduce X-ray data and perform spectral variability and broadband torus reflection modelling
recipe.method: Process XMM-Newton data with SAS and NuSTAR data with NUSTARDAS/HEASOFT; perform individual and simultaneous multi-epoch XMM-Newton spectral fits and combined XMM-Newton+NuSTAR broadband spectral fits using pexrav and borus02 torus reflection models in XSPEC.
key_parameters: XMM source radius = 35 arcsec, background radius = 70 arcsec, min 25 counts/bin; NuSTAR source radius = 50 arcsec, min 20 counts/bin; Fe Kalpha E = 6.4 keV, sigma = 0.01 keV; pexrav E_cut = 100 keV; borus02 half-opening angle fixed to 25 deg
assumptions: Galactic NH fixed to FTOOLS NH prediction; scattered power-law normalisation <= 1% of nuclear component; torus half-opening angle = 25 deg from BLR modelling

score_reason: All raw datasets are public and the optical/X-ray analysis steps and software versions are well documented, but ALMA processing details are omitted (relying on García-Burillo et al. 2021), custom IDL scripts for IFU deconvolution/toy modelling are not released, and the treated GMOS cube requires a web request.
rediscovery_reason: All primary raw data (GMOS, XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, HST, ALMA) are public in standard archives, and the main quantitative results (optical line fluxes/ratios, BLR ring parameters, CLOUDY distances, and XSPEC/borus02 torus parameters) are clearly tabulated.
